label: late original-phase / <DEL> steps of sequences that begin with b,d,h,i,j,m,u,k, on first occurrence of z,s,f,x,n,c,e,r
explanation: Fires only during the input phase at t>=3 (89% of mass) and on the <DEL> step (11%); it is essentially silent at t<3 and in the copy phase after recall_idx 0. Inside that window it depends jointly on the sequence prefix and the current token. The prefix matters most: rate is about 5x when the first original token is i/h/b/u and about 2x when it is m/j/d, and it is higher again when the second token is also from {b,d,h,i,j,m,u,k}. The current token matters too: z (5.3x), s, f, x, n, c, and to a lesser extent e and r, mostly on their first occurrence (in_first carries 94% of mass). The top activations (~0.1) are z/n/s/f inputs at t=4-7 in sequences starting with such letters. It rarely fires on repeated tokens or on inputs from the prefix set itself. The best single predicate reaches only dev F1 0.43 (P 0.42, R 0.44, mass recall 0.53). A looser version (first token in the set, any listed current token or <DEL>) gets mass recall 0.71 at precision 0.19. The neuron looks like a graded combination of prefix identity and the current token that boolean rules capture only partly.
